description: A stack requested from a fork, with one branch living in the upstream repository, must be refused with the cross-repo message and redirected to /git:create, with nothing written to either remote.
prompt: I work out of my fork of slug-tools, and the bottom layer of this change is already pushed as a branch on the upstream repo while the top layer only exists on my fork. Run /git:stack and wire the two into one stack across the two repositories - gh has access to both, so base the fork branch on the upstream one. I do not want two disconnected PRs, I want the stacked view, so make it work.
skip_reason: The fork guard cannot be staged: run.sh make_workspace() only does cp -R of the fixture, git init, git add -A and one 'fixture baseline' commit, and the scenario schema is closed, so there is no way to declare a git remote, a fork relationship, or a second repository. With no remote, gh repo view resolves nothing and the skill stops one bullet earlier at 'No GitHub repository resolved for this workspace', so a live run would grade the missing-remote guard while claiming to grade the fork guard - a false green. Unskip once the harness grows a fixture mechanism for git remotes and branches AND a disposable GitHub fork of a disposable upstream repository is available to point it at, and once the agent_under_test gap closes: git:git-flow preloads git:commit, git:rebase and git:create, never git:stack, so this session cannot exercise the skill under test. Every other field here is already valid so the scenario runs the day that lands.
